sanskrit: dadāmīty eva brūyād anu cainām abhutsata | vaśāṃ brahmabhyo yācadbhyas tat prajāvad apatyavat ||
english: He should simply say "I give," and then accompany her; the cow given to the Brahmins who ask for her — that act yields offspring and progeny.

sanskrit: prajayā sa vi krīṇīte paśubhiś copa dasyati | ya ārṣeyebhyo yācadbhyo devānāṃ gāṃ na ditsati ||
english: He pays with his offspring and wastes away his cattle — he who refuses to give the cow of the gods to those sages who ask for her.

sanskrit: kūṭayāsya saṃ śīryante śroṇayā kāṭam ardati | baṇḍayā dahyante gṛhāḥ kāṇayā jīyate svam ||
english: By the deformed cow his bones crumble; by the lame cow he is ground down at the joint; by the mutilated cow his houses burn; by the one-eyed cow his property is lost.

sanskrit: vilohito adhiṣṭhānāc chakno vindati gopatim | tathā vaśāyāḥ sāṃvidyaṃ duradabhnā hy ucyase ||
english: From the standing-place of the red-spotted one, the dog finds the cow-owner — such is the covenant of the vaśā cow; for she is truly called the hard-to-deceive.

sanskrit: yo asyāḥ karṇāv āskunoty ā sa deveṣu vṛścate | lakṣma kurva iti manyate kanīyaḥ kṛṇute svam ||
english: He who clips her ears is cut off among the gods; he thinks he is merely making a mark, but he diminishes his own fortune.

sanskrit: pador asyā adhiṣṭhānād viklindur nāma vindati | anāmanāt saṃ śīryante yā mukhenopajighrati ||
english: From the place where her hooves stand, he obtains the disease called viklindu; the limbs of one who sniffs her from the front crumble.

sanskrit: yad asyā gopatau satyā loma dhvāṅkṣo ajīhiḍat | tataḥ kiśorā mriyante vatsāṃś ca ghātuko vṛkaḥ ||
english: When a crow truly defiled the hair of the vaśā cow while she was in her owner's keeping, from that act the colts die and the wolf, the killer, takes the calves.

sanskrit: yad asyāḥ kasmai cid bhogāya bālān kaś cit pra kṛntati | tataḥ kumārā mriyante yakṣmaś chantsaty anāmanāt ||
english: If someone cuts her tail-hairs for his own enjoyment, from that act the young boys die and disease strikes through the limbs.

sanskrit: yad asyāḥ palpulanāya śakṛd dāsī samasyati | tato 'pirūpaṃ jāyate tasmād avyeṣyad enasaḥ ||
english: If a slave woman gathers her dung for use as fuel, from that a misbegotten child is born; therefore one should keep away from this transgression.

sanskrit: jāyamānābhi jāyate devān sabrāhmaṇān vaśā | tasmād brahmabhyo deyaiṣā tad āhuḥ svasya gopanam ||
english: At birth the vaśā cow is born together with the gods and Brahmins; therefore she must be given to the Brahmins — that, they say, is the protection of one's own welfare.

sanskrit: ya enāṃ vanim āyanti teṣāṃ devakṛtā vaśā | brahmajyeyaṃ tad abruvan ya enāṃ nipriyāyate ||
english: The vaśā cow, made by the gods, belongs to those who come to her as petitioners; what they called "robbing the Brahmins" is what he does who dishonors her.

sanskrit: ya enāṃ yācadbhya ārṣeyebhyo na ditsati | ā sa deveṣu vṛścate brāhmanānāṃ ca manyave ||
english: He who refuses to give her to those sage-born petitioners is cut off among the gods and faces the wrath of the Brahmins.

sanskrit: yasyānyaḥ syād vaśābhogo anyām iccheta tarhi saḥ | hiṃsyād adattā gopatiṃ yācitāṃ ca na ditsati ||
english: He whose enjoyment of the vaśā cow belongs to another — if he desires a different one then — the unbestowed cow would harm the owner, for he refuses to give away the one that has been asked for.

sanskrit: yathā śevadhir nihito brāhmaṇānāṃ tathā vaśā | tām etad ā yanti yasmin kasmiṃś ca jāyate ||
english: Just as a treasure is laid up belonging to the Brahmins, so is the vaśā cow; they come to her wherever and in whatever family she is born.

sanskrit: svam etad ā yanti yad vaśāṃ brāhmaṇā abhi | yathaitān anyaj jinīyād evāsyānirodhanam ||
english: When the Brahmins approach the vaśā cow, they come to what is their own; just as one would win over another through this — such is the means of not obstructing her.

sanskrit: cared evā traihāyaṇād avijñātagadā satī | vaśāṃ ca vidyān nārada brāhmaṇas tarhy eṣyaḥ ||
english: She should roam freely for three years, being a true cow whose ailment is unrecognized; and then, O Nārada, one should identify the vaśā cow — then is the Brahmin to come for her.

sanskrit: ya enām avaśām āha devānāṃ nihitaṃ nidhim | ubhau tasmai bhavāśarvau parikramyeṣum asyataḥ ||
english: He who calls her unsuitable — this treasure laid down by the gods — both Bhava and Śarva circle around him and shoot their arrows at him.

sanskrit: duradabhnainam ā śaye yācitāṃ ca na ditsati | nāsmai kāmaḥ sam ṛdhyate yam adattvā cikīrṣati ||
english: The hard-to-deceive one lies in wait for him who refuses to give the one that was asked for; no desire of his prospers — whatever he wishes to accomplish without giving her.

sanskrit: yo asyā ūdho na veda- -atho asyā stanān uta | ubhayenaivaināṃ duhe dātuṃ ced aśakad vaśām ||
english: He who knows neither her udder nor her teats — yet by both means he milks her — if only he had been able to give the vaśā cow.

sanskrit: devā vaśāṃ yācanti mukhaṃ kṛtvā brahmaṇam | teṣāṃ sarveṣām adadad dheḍaṃ ny eti mānuṣaḥ ||
english: The gods ask for the vaśā cow, taking on the form of Brahmins; the mortal who does not give to all of them falls into their displeasure.

sanskrit: heḍaṃ paśūnāṃ ny eti brāhmaṇebhyo 'dadad vaśām | devānāṃ nihitaṃ bhāgaṃ martyaś cen nipriyāyate ||
english: He falls into the displeasure of the cattle — he who has not given the vaśā cow to the Brahmins; if a mortal dishonors the share that the gods have laid away.

sanskrit: yad anye śataṃ yāceyur brāhmaṇā gopatiṃ vaśām | athaitā devā abruvann evaṃ ha viduṣo vaśā ||
english: Even if a hundred Brahmins were to ask the cow-owner for the vaśā cow — then the gods declared: "Such is the vaśā of a knowing man."

sanskrit: ya evaṃ viduṣe 'dattvā- -anyasmai dadad vaśām | durgā tasmā adhiṣṭhānе pṛthivī sahadevatā ||
english: He who, without giving to such a knowing man, gives the vaśā cow to another — for him the earth with all her deities becomes a place of hardship.

sanskrit: devā vaśām ayācan yasminn agre ajāyata | tām etāṃ vidyān nāradaḥ saha devair ud ājata ||
english: The gods begged for the vaśā cow from the one in whose family she was first born; this one Nārada recognized, and he led her out together with the gods.

sanskrit: anapatyam alpapaśuṃ vaśā kṛṇotu pūruṣam | brāhmaṇaiś ca yācitām athaināṃ ni priyāyate ||
english: May the vaśā cow render a man childless and poor in cattle — he who dishonors her even when she has been asked for by Brahmins.

sanskrit: agnīṣomābhyāṃ kāmāya mitrāya varuṇāya ca | tebhyo yācanti brāhmaṇās tebhya ā vṛścate 'dadhat ||
english: For Agni-and-Soma, for Kāma, for Mitra and for Varuṇa — the Brahmins ask in their name; he who does not give is cut off from them.

sanskrit: yāvad asyā gopatir na- -upaśṛṇuyād ṛcaḥ svayam | cared asya tāvad goṣu nāsya śrutā gṛhe syāt ||
english: As long as the owner of the vaśā cow himself has not listened to the sacred verses, she may roam among his cattle for that time — but she would not be as one heard of in his house.

sanskrit: yo asyā ṛca upaśrutya- -atha goṣv acīcarat | āyuś ca tasya bhūtiṃ ca devā vṛścanti hīḍitāḥ ||
english: He who, having listened to the sacred verses about her, then lets her wander among ordinary cattle — the gods, angered, cut short both his life and his prosperity.

sanskrit: vaśā carantī bahudhā devānāṃ nihito nidhiḥ | āviṣkṛṇute rūpāṇi yathā sthāma jigāṃsati ||
english: The vaśā cow, roaming in many ways, is the treasure laid down by the gods; she reveals her forms according to whatever dwelling-place she desires to reach.

sanskrit: āvir ātmānaṃ kṛṇute yathā sthāma jigāṃsati | atho ha brahmabhyo vaśā yākyāya kṛṇute manaḥ ||
english: She makes herself manifest according to whatever dwelling-place she desires to reach; and so the vaśā cow turns her mind to the Brahmins for the purpose of being asked for.
